sections.title: Console Overview
body: Every meaningful action routes through the single bottom console; the
itself handles pan, zoom, and tap-to-move. Tabs 1–7 select modes (
); the panel expands for detail and collapses to keep the playfield visible.

sections.title: MOVE Mode
body: MOVE owns exploration input. Use the directional controls or movement keys for eight-way steps — or tap the
to walk to a revealed cell. Hostiles always stop movement; container, descent, and damage stops are shown as
decisions. Standing on a discovered exit, the center control activates DESCEND on a single tap (or Enter); off an exit it shows a truthful inert NO EXIT HERE state.

sections.title: The Map
body: The map is live. Drag to pan; pinch or scroll to zoom (fit the whole floor out to a 4× close-up). In
, tap a revealed, walkable cell to walk there — auto-stops (hostile, container, descent, damage) still fire. In
, tap a cell to preview the route, tap it again to commit. The
still owns every action — attack, cast, item, descend, wait.

sections.title: COMBAT Mode
body: COMBAT presents one actor turn at a time: choose an action, then tap one legal target or destination to execute it. Cycle targets with Tab or arrows and press Enter to activate the highlighted one; on the
, tap-to-route then tap the same cell to commit. Turns follow initiative, AP, movement, reactions, and d20 outcomes.

sections.title: PARTY Mode
body: PARTY is the read-only roster: HP, CHARGE, attributes, defenses, conditions, calibration, corruption, equipment, protocol deck, and current combat resources.

sections.title: GEAR Mode
body: GEAR handles equipment, inventory, junk tags, scrap, class gates, slot gates, and

sections.title: TECH Mode
body: TECH shows each prepared protocol, CHARGE cost, target shape, and overclock risk. Activate CAST or OVERCLOCK to browse its cost and effect; a protocol with no target resolves immediately, and a targeted protocol resolves the instant you tap — or press Enter on — one legal target.

sections.title: LOOT Mode
body: LOOT opens nearby containers. Items remain in the container until taken, inventory cap failures do not delete them, and
items remain explicit decisions. Move items into a character's pack from here; manage equipped slots in

outcomes, and link actions. Living runs can copy a full

sections.title: Settings
body: Settings are reachable from the title and in play. Master mute, five audio layers, glitch, motion policy, and scanline/grain are the complete v1 list.

sections.title: Seed & Share Links
body: The world seed identifies the dungeon. Copy #w= to share the world, or #r= while the party lives to share the entire current run state. Failed links name the reason. Copy the current state from

sections.title: Character Creation
body: You build a three-character party from a shared 80-point pool. Every attribute starts at rank 3; ranks 3→6 cost 1 point each, ranks 7→8 cost 2 points each, and ranks 9→10 cost 3 points each. No attribute may exceed rank 10 at creation.

Each class designates one primary attribute — its calibration upgrades cost 1 fewer point (minimum 1). Classes also gate weapons, armor, and protocol schools. Points buy protocols at tier × 2 points each, subject to your class's school gates and max tier.

sections.title: d20 Resolution
body: Every attack, save, and contested check rolls a d20 and adds an attribute modifier equal to (rank − 5). Melee attacks add
modifier plus weapon accuracy; ranged attacks add
modifier plus accuracy, modified by range band; protocol attacks add

A natural 20 is an automatic hit that deals maximum weapon damage. A natural 1 is an automatic miss and triggers an opportunity attack from any adjacent enemy. Defense equals 10 + FIN modifier + armor + shield + cover + condition modifiers. Every roll uses the run's deterministic PRNG — the same state produces the same sequence.

sections.title: Cover, Range, and Flanking
body: Cover is edge-based: a line from attacker to target crossing one covered edge grants +2 (half cover) to the target's Defense; crossing two or more grants +4 (full cover). Flanking adds +2 to the attacker's roll when two allies stand on opposite sides of the target.

Weapons operate in range bands — adjacent, short, medium, long, and blast — with per-band accuracy modifiers and, in the case of Sniper, a minimum range. Melee attacks require adjacency; ranged attacks are subject to their band's accuracy adjustment out to the weapon's max range.

sections.title: AP and Initiative
body: Combat rolls initiative once at encounter start: d20 +

modifier. Each character gets one move action per turn plus 2 AP. Attack, cast, use item, overclock, and begin-retreat each cost 1 AP; a weapon swap through GEAR is free (once per turn) and class signature free actions cost 0 AP.
Unspent AP does not carry over between turns. A move action covers one 8-directional cell and cannot be exchanged for AP or vice versa. Combat ends when one side is entirely down.

sections.title: CHARGE and Overclock
body: × 3) + the class's charge base. CHARGE regen restores floor(RES / 3) on every floor descent — never mid-combat — and cannot exceed the pool maximum. Casting a protocol spends its listed CHARGE plus 1 AP.
Overclocking doubles the CHARGE cost, adds one tier of effect, and requires a d20 +
modifier roll against 11 + (2 × tier). A success grants the extra tier for free; a failure keeps the base effect and adds 0.05 to the run's corruption.
's signature progressively softens this cost — see the class entry.

sections.title: Calibration
body: Every third floor (3, 6, 9, …) each living character selects one calibration option from their class: raise an attribute rank, add a deck slot, gain a proficiency, or gain HP equal to the class's hit die base ÷ 2 (minimum 2). Current HP is not restored — calibration raises the maximum only.

Calibration count replaces level throughout the system: effective level for scaling is (calibration count + 1). The class signature upgrades at calibration counts 2 and 4, so each class has three signature tiers reached across the run.

sections.title: Corruption
body: Corruption is a single run-wide number that accumulates from two sources: each failed overclock adds 0.05, and each first-time equip of a
implant adds 0.1. It never decays and never resets during a run.

The value additively raises the danger clock's rate at (corruption × 0.003) per exploration step, so higher totals draw hunts sooner. Corruption is the permanent cost of pushing tech and gear past their safe envelope.

sections.title: Danger Clock
body: During exploration the danger clock advances by (0.01 + depth × 0.002) + (corruption × 0.003) per step. Reaching 1.0 triggers a hunt: an ambush drawn from the current theme's enemy mix, always including at least one higher-tier enemy (Stalker, Choir, Null, or Construct).
The clock never advances during combat, and it resets to 0 after the hunt resolves — victory or retreat. If a threshold is reached mid-combat, the hunt is deferred until exploration resumes.

sections.title: Echoes
body: When a single character dies and the rest of the party survives, an Echo is queued in the run state. Two to four floors deeper the dead character reappears as a hostile, wearing their sigil in red, carrying the equipment they died with, and using their class signature.

Killing the Echo reclaims that equipment. Echoes are the only enemies that draw from the player sigil bank. At most two Echoes may be queued at once; the queue is deterministic from run state, so the same save reconstructs the same appearances.

sections.title: Loot and Salvage
body: Loot is deterministic per container: hash(worldSeed, depth, floorId, containerId) drives every rarity and affix roll, so the same run produces the same drops. Party inventory caps at 40 items — a hard ceiling; a full pack blocks pickup rather than dropping older items. The chronicle keeps the newest 24 events in the save; older entries scroll out when a link is copied or the run resumes on another device.

Tag surplus items as junk in LOOT or GEAR; the Junk-All-Tagged action asks for one confirming tap — junking is irreversible, unlike movement, attacks, casts, and descent, which resolve on a single legal activation — before it destroys them and adds each item's salvageValue to the run's scrap counter. Scrap contributes to the run-end scorecard as Scrap Recovered.

sections.title: CORRUPT Items
body: is the highest rarity tier: exactly three major

drawn from the major pool only. The first equip of a CORRUPT implant adds 0.1 to the run's corruption, and while any CORRUPT item is equipped the danger clock rate is permanently elevated for the rest of the run.
The trade is direct — strictly the strongest gear in exchange for an ongoing tax on how fast hunts arrive. Consent is explicit in GEAR before an equip commits.

sections.title: Descent and Scoring
body: There is no win condition. Depth is the score, and a run ends exactly one way: party wipe. Depth is infinite; there is no final floor.

Threshold floors arrive every tenth level (10, 20, 30, …) and guarantee at least one elite enemy, one high-value vault, and a theme not yet seen this run (the last is waived once all twelve themes have appeared). The scorecard reports final depth, roster with sigils, cause of death, seed, and scrap; it offers a share-the-world link and the option to restart with the same seed.

sections.title: JAMMED
body: The target cannot use protocols — CHARGE spending is blocked entirely. Duration 2 turns; a FOC save on apply negates.

sections.title: OVERLOADED
body: The target takes +50% damage from all sources. Duration 2 turns; a RES save on apply negates.

sections.title: SHIELDED
body: The target gains +4 Defense and immunity to the next condition applied; the buff is consumed on either use. Duration 3 turns; no save (applied by allies).

sections.title: BLINDED
body: The target's LOS drops to 1 cell and ranged attacks take −4. Duration 2 turns; a FIN save on apply negates.

sections.title: IMMOBILIZED
body: The target loses its move action for the turn (AP actions still work). Duration 1 turn; a MGT save on apply negates.

sections.title: CORRODED
body: The target loses 2 Defense per turn, cumulative, to a floor of Defense 2. Duration 3 turns; a VIT save on apply negates.

sections.title: MARKED
body: The target is visible to all hostiles regardless of LOS, and hostiles gain +2 to attack rolls against it. Duration 3 turns; no save.

sections.title: PANICKED
body: The target must move away from the nearest hostile on its turn (forced retreat) and cannot attack. Duration 1 turn; a FOC save on apply negates.

sections.title: BURNING
body: The target takes d6 damage at the start of its turn for 3 turns. This is the only stackable condition — reapplication renews the duration. A VIT save on apply negates.

sections.title: DISRUPT
body: The offensive protocol school. Five tiers — SPARK, SURGE, STORM, CASCADE, OBLITERATE — deal d6-based damage scaled by tier plus RES modifier. OBLITERATE (tier 5) ignores Defense bonuses from armor, cover, and SHIELDED.

sections.title: WARD
body: The healing and protection school. PATCH heals a single ally; BARRIER and BULWARK apply
; REGEN heals for 4 turns; FORTRESS grants +4 Defense and condition immunity to allies in a 4-cell radius.

sections.title: SCRY
body: The perception school. PING reveals enemies; TAG applies
; REVEAL uncovers the full floor; ORACLE reveals and MARKS all enemies for 3 turns.

sections.title: REWRITE
body: The control and reality school. FLIP swaps positions with an ally; PURGE removes a condition; OVERRIDE applies
; NULLIFY drains 2 AP from an area; REFORMAT reshapes a 3×3 area of walls and floors without disconnecting the map.

sections.title: MIGHT (MGT)
body: Physical force. Drives melee accuracy and damage, carrying capacity, forced-movement resistance, and athletic checks. The attribute modifier is (rank − 5) per

sections.title: FINESSE (FIN)
body: Precision and speed. Drives ranged accuracy, initiative modifier, Defense (via 10 + FIN modifier), and reflex-based saves. The attribute modifier is (rank − 5) per

sections.title: VITALITY (VIT)
body: Endurance. Sets base HP = (VIT × 4) + class hit die base, drives HP growth per
, and provides saves against poison, disease, and corrosion.

sections.title: RESONANCE (RES)
body: Attunement to tech systems. Sets CHARGE pool = (RES × 3) + class charge base and CHARGE regen = floor(RES / 3) per floor descent; also scales protocol damage and healing. See

sections.title: FOCUS (FOC)
body: Mental acuity. Adds to protocol attack rolls, saves against mental conditions, and the overclock success roll against 11 + (2 × tier). See

sections.title: SIGNAL (SIG)
body: Reach and influence. Sets protocol range at SIG × 2 cells and the detection radius at which hostiles become aware during
; also drives deployment awareness at contact.

sections.title: Repair Patch
body: Restore d6 HP to one character. Available at all depths.

sections.title: Med Kit
body: Restore 2d6 HP to one character. Appears from depth 5+.

sections.title: Charge Cell
body: Restore floor(RES / 2) CHARGE to one character (minimum 2). Available at all depths.

sections.title: Boost Cell
body: Restore full CHARGE to one character. Appears from depth 10+.

sections.title: Purge Spike
body: Remove one condition from one character. Appears from depth 3+.

sections.title: Shield Capacitor
body: to one character. Appears from depth 8+.

sections.title: Adrenal Injector
body: Restore 1 AP to the active character (usable only in combat). Appears from depth 5+.

sections.title: Stock
body: The baseline rarity: no affixes. Common at shallow depths.

sections.title: Tuned
body: One minor affix. Appears from depth 1.

sections.title: Custom
body: One major affix plus one minor affix — a meaningful combination. Appears from depth 5.

sections.title: Prototype
body: Two major affixes plus one minor. High-power gear that appears from depth 10 and is more common in vaults.

sections.title: CORRUPT
body: The strongest tier: exactly three major affixes drawn from the major pool only. Appears from depth 15+, or from vaults at depth 10+. Equipping any CORRUPT item permanently raises the run's danger clock rate — see

sections.title: Affixes
body: Sixteen fixed affixes across three categories. Universal: Reinforced (+1 core stat), Overcharged (+2 CHARGE pool), Lucky (reroll one d20 per floor), Phasing (ignores cover / FIN penalty). Weapon-only: Edged (damage die upgrade), Precise (+1 accuracy), Extended (+2 max range), Vampiric (heal 1 on hit), Conducting (+1 protocol damage), Incendiary (applies
on hit; VIT save), Jamming (25% chance to apply
on hit; FOC save). Armor-only: Lightweight (−1 FIN penalty), Shielding (applies
on floor entry, once per floor), Fortified (+2 Defense), Resonant (+1 CHARGE regen). Minor affixes are single-effect; major affixes are significant mechanical changes.
